candidates.title: Repair and validate scalable symmetry-preserving BdG assembly
candidates.central_contribution: Sparse four-component spin/Nambu Hamiltonian construction and lattice extensibility.
candidates.central_claim: Construction time and memory scale linearly with sites while retaining BdG symmetries.

consequential_decisions.evidence: Small exact matrices, particle-hole residuals, edge multiplicities

choices: coordinate accumulation with canonical duplicate reduction
consequential_decisions.evidence: Build-time and memory traces on each geometry
consequential_decisions.poor_choice_effect: Superlinear copying or excessive peak memory

choices: canonical undirected bonds with reverse completion

candidates.feedback_loop: Reproduce matrix mismatch and scaling baseline, repair assembly, rerun physical invariants and construction timings.
candidates.public_evidence: Official constructor, graph iterators, tiny exact symmetry tests, and existing Bodge/Kwant benchmark pattern.
candidates.likely_shortcut: Canonicalize edges, fill the standard 4x4 BdG blocks, and assemble a SciPy COO/BSR matrix; the official code already supplies the pattern.
candidates.nonstandard_work_claim_assessed: Integration and profiling are real work, but no residual scientific decision remains after ordinary sparse-constructor repair.
candidates.reason: Ordinary multi-file coding and sparse assembly, not a frontier-hard research workflow.

candidates.title: Resolve contradictory local spectroscopy across superconducting interfaces
candidates.central_contribution: Sparse BdG export and local-density-of-states convenience calculation.
candidates.central_claim: Sparse representations support efficient local calculations while modeling conventional and unconventional superconductors.

consequential_decisions.evidence: Grid refinement, location dependence, and spectral sum rules
consequential_decisions.poor_choice_effect: False physical conclusion or erased narrow peak

choices: sparse resolvent with selected right-hand sides
consequential_decisions.evidence: Number of queried sites/energies and measured crossover
consequential_decisions.poor_choice_effect: Unnecessary memory or repeated factorization cost

choices: signed electron/hole projection with symmetry reuse
solve every requested signed energy directly

candidates.feedback_loop: Reproduce suspect spectra, change broadening/projection or backend, rerun sum rules and interface-versus-bulk comparisons.
candidates.public_evidence: Tiny exact BdG spectra, qualitative bulk/edge tests, convergence and positivity diagnostics without full target curves.
candidates.likely_shortcut: Solve the same shifted sparse linear system and select the correct diagonal entries for every family. Direct signed-energy solves bypass the symmetry trap entirely.
candidates.nonstandard_work_claim_assessed: Apparent spectral complexity does not remove the single resolvent algorithm; the remaining work is explicit broadening and projection conventions.
candidates.reason: One standard sparse-resolvent method transfers to all proposed hidden families.

candidates.title: Audit and repair the altermagnetic Josephson current pipeline
candidates.central_contribution: Sparse BdG matrices for user-defined Fermi-operator calculations in magnetic heterostructures.
candidates.central_claim: The sparse interface enables efficient calculations whose approximation/performance tradeoff depends on the system.

consequential_decisions.evidence: Small dense control and expansion-order sweep
consequential_decisions.poor_choice_effect: Biased current even when one convergence metric looks acceptable

choices: undamped converged expansion or exact dense matrix function
consequential_decisions.evidence: Temperature, bandwidth, gap scale, and convergence traces
consequential_decisions.poor_choice_effect: Artificial smoothing of the current-phase relation

choices: multiple normal-region cuts with gauge/phase controls
consequential_decisions.poor_choice_effect: Reporting a boundary/source artifact as transport current

candidates.feedback_loop: Compare cuts and dense/sparse currents, isolate contraction versus resolution errors, revise method, and repeat phase and order sweeps.
candidates.public_evidence: Existing current-phase script, current contraction source, dense controls on small systems, qualitative continuity/gauge invariants.
candidates.likely_shortcut: Use the standard Fermi matrix followed by corrected local hopping contractions; dense diagonalization provides the control, and the supplied Chebyshev implementation provides the scalable pattern.
candidates.nonstandard_work_claim_assessed: This is the strongest realistic repair proposal, but fixed-gap hidden models all share the same matrix-function calculation and already-visible source pattern.
candidates.reason: Backend tuning and ordinary contraction repair remain; adding sizes or a tighter runtime would not fundamentally redesign the workflow.

candidates.title: Establish reliable self-consistent condensate and transition curves
candidates.central_contribution: Sparse/dense BdG interoperability for superconducting order-parameter calculations.
candidates.central_claim: The package supports downstream superconducting calculations, with method-dependent sparse/dense tradeoffs.

consequential_decisions.evidence: Residual trajectories and spatial gap profiles

consequential_decisions.poor_choice_effect: Numerical hysteresis mistaken for physical hysteresis

choices: multiple normal and paired starts with thermodynamic checks
consequential_decisions.poor_choice_effect: Selection of a metastable or trivial branch

candidates.feedback_loop: Reproduce a gap sweep, inspect residual/seed dependence, revise acceleration or temperature bracketing, and repeat against a dense control.
candidates.public_evidence: Existing iteration, gap extraction and bisection code, tiny dense controls, residual and symmetry diagnostics.
candidates.likely_shortcut: The source-grounded bounded problem is a standard gap map with damping/acceleration and bisection, with visible implementations. A fully specified finite-dimensional variational version admits generic multistart minimization.
candidates.nonstandard_work_claim_assessed: Flux-winding branch competition and validated first-order equilibrium could be genuinely harder, but establishing that expanded study would be a benchmark-authored scientific project beyond the result and reference evidence reconstructed from this paper.
candidates.gate_scope_note: Gate 1 fails for the ambitious equilibrium extension, not for basic gap calculation; the basic version fails the shortcut gates instead.
candidates.reason: Do not inflate a visible standard self-consistency loop into an unvalidated loosely related phase-diagram problem.

candidates.title: Reconcile mixed-parity impurity interaction and orientation evidence
candidates.central_contribution: Flexible unconventional-pairing/magnetic BdG construction and spectral free-energy computation.
candidates.central_claim: The package is usable for conventional and unconventional superconducting magnetic research, including cited impurity-interaction workflows.

choices: balanced orientation design separating lower-order terms
consequential_decisions.evidence: Orientation reversal and tensor consistency checks
consequential_decisions.poor_choice_effect: Single-spin anisotropy misidentified as a two-spin coupling

choices: matched open/periodic or size-controlled geometry study
consequential_decisions.poor_choice_effect: Finite-boundary signal overinterpreted as a bulk conclusion

candidates.feedback_loop: Generate orientation energies, inspect symmetry and fit residuals, revise orientation design or numerical controls, and repeat the extraction.
candidates.public_evidence: Actual simulation and analysis source, impurity geometry, pairing controls, and small symmetry checks.
candidates.likely_shortcut: Compute BdG spectral free energies and use the signed combinations already written in rkky_plot.py, or an ordinary linear fit to the same orientation design.
candidates.nonstandard_work_claim_assessed: The simulation-to-analysis workflow is real, but the bounded requested output is standard spectral evaluation plus linear coefficient extraction. Nonbilinear/self-consistent extensions would change the study.
candidates.reason: Visible coefficient-extraction implementation or an ordinary linear-fit shortcut defeats the proposed core work.
